talking_points.headline: HSBC names RedCoin stablecoin, will push it to 3.3m PayMe users before year-end
talking_points.context_html: HSBC has named its Hong Kong dollar stablecoin HSBC RedCoin and committed to launching it through PayMe and its HK mobile app before end-2026, giving a retail wallet with 3.3 million users a first regulated tokenised-money product. This moves the PayMe ecosystem story we have been tracking from AI-enabled merchant onboarding into digital assets proper. For Adam, a launch at this scale is a change-execution programme, not a product tweak — wallet integration, compliance workflow, controls and client education will all land on WPB's delivery agenda in Hong Kong.

talking_points.headline: Hong Kong's record HK$20bn digital green bond settles on HSBC Orion, with HSBC at every layer
talking_points.context_html: Hong Kong priced a record ~HK$20bn multi-currency digital green bond settled in tokenised deposits on HSBC Orion, with HSBC acting as platform provider, trustee and principal paying agent; Christopher Hui, Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury, tied it to the government's digital-asset policy push. Alongside the new Swift tokenised-deposit pilot with 17 banks, tokenised money is becoming shared market infrastructure rather than a series of one-off experiments. For Adam, HSBC's platform is now visibly core to Hong Kong's tokenised-market plumbing — that brings delivery, controls and regulatory-readiness work into WPB's orbit.

talking_points.headline: On Adam's desk: Avaloq goes live front-to-back at Gulf Bank's InvestGB — credit and RM desktop included
talking_points.context_html: InvestGB, the investment arm of Gulf Bank, went live front-to-back on Avaloq this week, covering wealth, portfolio, fund administration and credit/lending, with Avaloq's RM Workplace automating rebalancing and investment proposals for relationship managers — days after DBS deepened the same partnership. For Adam, this is the most directly useful external datapoint of the day: a referenceable go-live that combines credit on the Avaloq platform with an RM desktop doing automated proposals, squarely relevant to HSBC's own Avaloq Credit build and RM Workbench direction, and to how the platform's road map will serve both.

On Adam's Desk.title: Gulf Bank powers InvestGB with Avaloq platform in front-to-back go-live
On Adam's Desk.summary: InvestGB, the investment arm of Gulf Bank, has gone live front-to-back on Avaloq — unifying wealth, portfolio management, fund administration and credit/lending (including Lombard lending and collateral management), with Avaloq's RM Workplace giving RMs a unified client view and automated rebalancing and investment proposals. Akash Anand, MD for the Middle East, Africa and India at Avaloq, called it Avaloq's first client in Kuwait. It comes days after the DBS–Avaloq expansion we covered on 29 September, confirming convergence on the shared vendor stack. For Adam, a referenceable go-live with credit on the same platform — and an RM desktop doing automated proposals — is directly instructive for HSBC's own Avaloq Credit build and RM Workbench ambitions.

HSBC News.title: HSBC dubs its stablecoin for 3.3 million PayMe users RedCoin
HSBC News.summary: HSBC has named its Hong Kong dollar stablecoin HSBC RedCoin and plans to launch it before end-2026, initially through PayMe and its HK mobile app — putting the token inside a wallet with 3.3 million users. It extends the PayMe ecosystem push we covered last week (AI merchant onboarding) from payments into regulated digital assets, with the bank citing customer research showing 74% recognise at least one stablecoin use case. For Adam, this is a retail-scale digital-asset launch that will pull real change-execution demand: licensing conditions, wallet integration, compliance workflow and RM/client education across HK.

HSBC News.title: Hong Kong sets digital bond record with HK$20bn green issue settled on HSBC Orion
HSBC News.summary: Hong Kong priced a record ~HK$20bn-equivalent multi-currency digital green bond, settled in tokenised deposits on HSBC Orion — with HSBC as platform provider, trustee and principal paying agent alongside 13 banks. Christopher Hui, Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury, framed it as part of the government's drive to broaden tokenised use cases. The deal lands the same week as the Swift tokenised-deposit pilot and shows Orion becoming core market plumbing for HK's digital-asset ambitions. For Adam, HSBC's platform bet is now systemically visible — expect delivery, controls and regulatory-readiness work to follow inside WPB.

HSBC News.title: HSBC Private Bank: AI dominates agenda for entrepreneurs globally
HSBC News.summary: HSBC Private Bank's chief executive, appointed at the start of this year, says volatile markets and AI-driven change are opportunities rather than distractions for private bankers, as an entrepreneur-focused agenda shows AI dominating client conversations globally. The stance aligns PB's leadership narrative with the same AI-first direction HSBC has taken in staff-facing tooling. For Adam, it confirms the PB leadership tone he must convert into delivery: AI-enabled advisory and RM productivity are now the stated strategic centre, not a side experiment.

AI & Technology.title: Swift builds global payment rail linking fiat and tokenized deposits as 17 banks pilot
AI & Technology.summary: Seventeen banks across six continents — including HSBC, Standard Chartered and UBS — are piloting tokenised deposit transactions on a new Swift ledger built on Hyperledger, bridging fiat and tokenised money rails. The pilot signals the industry's interbank settlement layer moving toward tokenised formats, with DBS and Citi already testing cross-border tokenised payments. For Adam, tokenised money is shifting from pilots to shared infrastructure; banks that treat it as a change programme rather than a tech experiment will set the standards RM and product teams inherit.

Competitor Intelligence.title: Ping An Digital Bank reports growth in assets and deposits, wealth fee income up sevenfold
Competitor Intelligence.summary: Ping An Digital Bank grew assets 133% to over HK$15.6 billion by 30 June 2026, while wealth services lifted fee income sevenfold — a digital-only challenger scaling wealth monetisation in HSBC's home market. The numbers show HK virtual banks moving from deposit gathering into serious wealth distribution. For Adam, a cloud-native competitor compounding wealth fee income at this pace raises the bar for HSBC and HASE digital wealth journeys and their delivery cadence.

Private Banking & Wealth.title: Allianz Global Wealth Report 2026: markets drive record wealth as AI raises the stakes
Private Banking & Wealth.summary: Allianz's Global Wealth Report 2026 records Singapore households' net financial assets up 9.5% to €1.1 trillion, keeping the city-state 4th globally in per-capita wealth, with Taiwan 5th — APAC wealth pools deepening on the back of market gains. The report frames AI as the next wealth-creation stakes-raiser. For Adam, the structural growth of SG/TW wealth underpins the case for prioritising delivery capacity in those booking centres, including the market PDC model currently being designed.

Regulatory & Markets.title: RBC's Chiriseri says 30-year Treasury yield at 6% is possible
Regulatory & Markets.summary: Rufaro Chiriseri, head of fixed income for Europe at RBC Wealth Management, told Bloomberg that 6% on the 30-year US Treasury is 'not wildly out of any possibility' and that yields could keep trending higher. Higher-for-longer US rates would pressure bond portfolios and shape client allocation conversations across APAC wealth books. For Adam, sustained rate volatility keeps demand alive for the structured and advice-led journeys WPB is building, and it is a backdrop risk to test delivery assumptions against.
